prediction:
THOUGHT: A young woman with long-standing common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) and multiple autoimmune manifestations developed bilateral vision symptoms with multifocal choroidal infiltrates, no anterior chamber, vitreous, or retinal inflammation, and a transvitreal aspirate showing scant lymphocytes and histiocytes but no organisms or malignant cells. Microbiologic studies of aspirate, blood and urine were negative. The lesions (including a large right macular choroidal infiltrate with overlying subretinal fluid) resolved over ~3 months with resultant chorioretinal scarring. Taken together these features favor an immune-mediated inflammatory choroidopathy rather than infection or malignancy: CVID is associated with dysregulated autoimmunity, the biopsy showed inflammatory cells without organisms or malignant cells, and rapid resolution after immunomodulatory therapy supports an autoimmune etiology. Infectious choroiditis (TB, fungal, syphilis) and intraocular lymphoma or metastatic disease remain important alternatives but are less likely given negative microbiology and tissue studies and the clinical response.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Autoimmune choroidopathy — multifocal inflammatory choroiditis (e.g., autoimmune/multifocal choroiditis in the CVID setting; PIC/MFC-spectrum)
2. Infectious choroiditis/granulomatous choroiditis (occult TB, fungal, or syphilitic choroiditis) — less likely given negative testing
3. Primary choroidal/uveal lymphoma (intraocular lymphoma involving the choroid) — can present with subtle cells on biopsy and mimic inflammation
4. Sarcoid-associated choroiditis (granulomatous choroid involvement from sarcoidosis)
5. Choroidal metastasis (metastatic tumor to the choroid)

Case Information:
A woman in her mid-20s with common variable immune deficiency (CVID) for 11 years, with history of frequent infectious disease and autoimmune conditions including dermatitis, pancreatitis, colitis, cerebritis, and lung disease. She was managed with antibiotics, corticosteroids, and immune globulin therapy. For 3 weeks, she noted bilateral ocular pain and blurred vision.

Physical Examination:
Visual acuity was 20/200 OD and 20/25 OS. The anterior segment, vitreous, and retina demonstrated no inflammation. Ophthalmoscopy revealed multifocal choroidal infiltrates in each eye. Right eye infiltration measured 14 mm at base, 3.9-mm thickness, with overlying subretinal fluid plus additional tiny multifocal sites. Left eye showed multifocal small choroidal infiltrates of 0.5-mm diameter.

Diagnostic Tests:
- Biopsy: Transvitreous fine-needle aspiration biopsy of macular lesion in right eye showed scant lymphocytes and histiocytes, with no evidence of fungus, bacteria, or malignant cells.- Microbiological studies: Tests of tumor aspirate, blood, and urine samples showed no infection.- Imaging:  Image Title: Figure 1. Autoimmune Choroidopathy  Image Description: A-D shows choroidopathy on ophthalmoscopy. E and F show optical coherence tomography findings.  Image Title: Figure 2. Resolution After Treatment  Image Description: Findings after 3 months showing resolution of choroidal infiltration, with chorioretinal scar at biopsy site in right eye, less apparent focal choroidal inflammatory sites in left eye, resolution of subretinal fluid with residual precipitates in right eye, and normal findings in left eye.
